Harry Halliday (born **1855**, exact date unknown; died **1931**) was an Australian cricketer who played first-class cricket in the late 19th century. Here’s what is known about him:

### **Early Life & Background**
- Born in **Victoria, Australia**, likely in or around **Melbourne**.
- Little is known about his early life, but he emerged as a promising cricketer in the 1870s and 1880s.

### **Cricket Career**
- **First-Class Debut**: Halliday made his first-class debut for **Victoria** in the **1877–78 season** against **New South Wales** at the **Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)**.
- **Batting Style**: A **right-handed batsman**, he was known for his aggressive strokeplay.
- **Key Performances**:
  - In his debut match (1877–78), he scored **31** and **10**, showing early promise.
  - His highest first-class score was **52** for Victoria against **Tasmania** in **1884–85**.
  - He played **11 first-class matches** between **1877 and 1885**, scoring **243 runs at an average of 12.15**.
  - He also took **3 wickets** with his **right-arm medium pace** bowling.
- **Domestic Cricket**: Played for **Melbourne Cricket Club (MCC)** and was a regular in Victorian cricket during his era.
- **Intercolonial Matches**: Represented Victoria in **intercolonial matches** (precursors to the Sheffield Shield) against New South Wales and Tasmania.

### **Later Life & Death**
- After retiring from first-class cricket in the mid-1880s, Halliday continued playing **club cricket** in Melbourne.
- He worked as a **cricketer and groundsman** at the **MCG** in his later years.
- Died in **1931** in **Melbourne, Victoria**, at the age of **76**.

### **Legacy**
- While not one of Australia’s most famous cricketers, Halliday was part of the **early generation of Victorian cricketers** who helped establish the game in Australia.
- His career overlapped with the **early years of Test cricket** (the first Test was in 1877), though he never played at that level.

- **ESPNcricinfo** ([www.espncricinfo.com](https://www.espncricinfo.com))
